471: Comparison with Saengdeejing et al. 2026 (npj Comput. Mater. 12, 362, Pt–Rh) (npj_ptrh/COMPARISON.md): harmonic phonons of the ordered phases and SQS mixing energies taken from Matlantis PFP and DFT, fitted to CALPHAD parameters in Thermo-Calc, i.e. a "computation-only TDB" (same family as PhaseForge; the liquid is an ideal solution). The MLIP and DFT order–disorder transition temperatures agree within about 50 K. The differences from this project are the liquid (TI or not), the finite-temperature treatment of the solid phases (harmonic phonons + Neumann–Kopp vs QHA/TI) and the way the phase diagram is built (CALPHAD fit vs convex hull). ORCHID has no literature values for Pt–Rh, only 3 SGTE assessments (fcc + liquid) and 3 points from a hand-drawn diagram; that hand-drawn diagram places an fcc two-phase separation at 605 K, whereas the paper finds no miscibility gap.
472: Pt–Rh with universal MLIPs (11-04 to 06, ftphase/examples/ptrh/): stages 01–07 (13 random fcc compositions, defect cells of the ordered phases PtRh "40", PtRh₃ and Pt₃Rh + sublattice entropy, 7 liquids 2500→1900 K) completed on mygarden6 with GRACE-2L, NequIP-OAM-M and MACE-MPA-0. The decisive quantity is the 0 K energy difference "ordered phase − random fcc": the paper's DFT gives about −11 meV/atom for PtRh, MACE-MPA-0 −7 to −12 and SevenNet-MF-ompa −11 (0 K screen), whereas GRACE-2L and NequIP-OAM-M give 0 ± 2 (their random fcc mixing is too deep at −30 meV). In the solids-only low-temperature re-assembly (assemble_lowT.py) the PtRh ordering of MACE-MPA-0 falls at 230–240 K (paper: PFP 258 K, DFT 210 K), but PtRh₃ and Pt₃Rh cannot be resolved because their ordering energies are below the configuration noise (a few meV), and all ordered phases of GRACE-2L and NequIP are fit noise. On the melting side QHA overstabilises (Pt 2300–2410 K vs 2041), so solid TI is pending. Lesson: the defect-cell + sublattice-entropy treatment of ordered phases is unusable once the ordering energy drops below about 5 meV; switch to CE+MC there.
473: Pt–Rh solid-phase diagram and CE+MC ordering temperatures (2026-11-07 to 08)
474: The WorkChain assembly only gridded "temperatures with at least 3 liquid compositions", so the Pt–Rh ordering window (100–300 K) was missing from the output. On 11-07/08 assemble_diagram gained allow_solid_only (temperatures without a liquid use the solids-only convex hull), the WorkChain's solids_ti gained composition/cell filters (x, keys, one_per_x), and run_aiida.py --solid-only --ends-ti submitted a "solids only + 2,048-atom TI of the end members" WorkChain for 3 MLIPs (MACE pk 11345, GRACE-2L 11358, NequIP-OAM-M 11372, running). Fig. 10 is the solid-phase diagram re-assembled beforehand from the existing 05 table with the liquid removed (ptrh/assemble_lowT.py; the same temperatures at the quantum harmonic level).
475: Fig. 10. Solids-only T–x diagram of Pt–Rh (100–1000 K, classical QHA + CEF-type sublattice entropy, ptrh/out/solid_panels.png). The dashed line at 210 K is the paper's DFT, the dotted line at 258 K the PFP fcc↔PtRh ordering temperature. The only physical band is the PtRh of MACE-MPA-0 (x 0.44–0.56) surviving up to 230 K; the PtRh₃ at 910 K, fcc+fcc and the ordered phases of GRACE-2L and NequIP are all fits of configuration noise.
476: Fig. 10b. Fig. 10 with the configuration-noise fits removed (ptrh/solid_panels_filtered.py → ptrh/out/solid_panels_filtered.png, 2026-11-10). Ordered phases are kept only for the MLIPs whose 0 K ordering energy E(ordered) − E(random fcc) is −7 meV/atom or below (table of result 1; random-cell noise about 5 meV/atom), and same-phase segments (fcc+fcc, PtRh+PtRh) are dropped. What remains is only PtRh+fcc of MACE-MPA-0 and SevenNet-MF-ompa (200–230 K, SevenNet up to 270 K); for GRACE-2L and NequIP-OAM-M every segment is dropped (0 to 9 of 549–661 segments). ▼ marks the CE + canonical MC transition temperatures (Fig. 11).
477: Fig. 10c. The paper's phase diagrams (Saengdeejing, Sahara, Kino, Kawazoe, Higashino, Chikyow, npj Comput. Mater. 12, 362 (2026), Figs. 9–11, CC BY 4.0, cropped from papers/s41524-026-02212-9.pdf p. 7–8, ptrh/out/paper_fig{9,10,11}.png). Left: the DFT TDB; middle: comparison of the MLIP (solid) and DFT (dashed) between −200 and 100 °C; right: the MLIP (PFP) TDB. The liquid is an ideal solution with no liquid data. The ordering window (−130 to −15 °C = 146–258 K) is at the same position as the MACE/SevenNet bands in Fig. 10b.
478: Fig. 10d. The Pt–Rh phase diagram that can be drawn from the databases, with the solid phases added, over the full temperature range (ptrh/overlay_full.py → ptrh/out/overlay_ptrh_full.png; the vertical axis is broken between 100–400 K and 1700–2400 K). Top row, solid–liquid: the PtRh-98Jac boundaries (black lines) of the 3 SGTE assessments in ORCHID-Diagrams (PtRh-98Jac, 02Mam, 98Spe-LB, all fcc + liquid only, Pt 2041 K → Rh 2237 K, no invariant reaction; orchid_calphad/sgte_diagrams.py --systems ptrh, out/sgte_ptrh.png) overlaid on the 4 MLIPs in the WorkChain's liquid window (1910–2400 K, taking the run with end-member TI where one exists). Bottom row, solids: the databases have no ordered phases, so the reference column shows the invariant reactions of the paper's Table 7 as line segments (PFP solid, DFT dashed: fcc↔PtRh 258/211 K, fcc↔PtRh₃ 235/156 K, fcc↔Pt₃Rh 146 K, eutectoids 146 K and 211/149 K), and the MLIP columns overlay the solids-only re-assembly with the same noise-removal rule as Fig. 10b and the CE+MC transition temperatures (▼). Between 400 K and 1910 K it is single-phase fcc (also for the MLIPs: nothing survives the noise removal). ORCHID has no Pt–Rh literature values (COMPARISON.md), so only the solid–liquid band is the "database phase diagram". The MLIPs put the solid–liquid region 100–500 K low on the Pt side, and the PtRh ordering of MACE and SevenNet falls between the paper's DFT and PFP (200–270 K). The old figure with only the liquid window is orchid_calphad/out/overlay_ptrh.png.
479: Because the defect-cell method fails for systems with ordering energies of the 5 meV class, CE + canonical MC (ptrh/ce_mc.py, outside AiiDA) was run with MACE-MPA-0 and SevenNet-MF-ompa: 631 fcc configurations enumerated with icet and relaxed with the MLIP, a least-squares CE (41 ECI, CV 0.5–0.7 meV/atom), and canonical MC on 2,048 sites cooled from 500 to 20 K, taking the peak of C_v (Fig. 11).
480: Fig. 11. CE + canonical MC with MACE-MPA-0 (out_ce_mace-mpa-0/cv.png): left C_v, right formation energy. Transitions at 160 K for x_Rh = 0.5, 140 K for 0.75 and 100 K for 0.25. SevenNet-MF-ompa gives 180 / 120 / 120 K (at 0.5 a first-order-like C_v peak of 9 k_B).
490: The PtRh ordering of both MLIPs is at 160–180 K, 30–100 K below the paper. Two effects contribute: the CE ordering energies (MACE −7.4, SevenNet −7.1 meV/atom) are shallower than the DFT value of about −11, and the CEF (Bragg–Williams) gives a higher T_c than MC (230 vs 160 K for the same MACE).
491: The A₃B types could not be resolved by the defect-cell method, but CE+MC shows clear peaks at 120–140 K. An ECI-based method free of configuration noise is the only practical route at ordering energies of this size.
492: Inside and outside AiiDA: stages 01–07 and the end-member TI are inside the WorkChain (with provenance); the 0 K screening, CE+MC and the low-temperature re-assembly are still external scripts.
493: Ni–Al and Ag–Cu with 3 MLIPs: phase diagrams with 2,000-atom TI for the solid phases (2026-10-30 to 11-06)
494: The WorkChains of example 7 (Ni–Al) and example 9 (Ag–Cu) were run with GRACE-FS-OAM, GRACE-1L-OMAT (fp32) and SevenNet-0 (user choice: the 3 fast ones). At first the solid phases were computed with QHA only, but the fcc Al of GRACE-FS and SevenNet-0 and the B2 of all three did not melt even at 2000 K, so the result could not be compared with the EAM diagrams. The solid phases were therefore replaced by 2,048–3,456-atom calphy TI with mlip_solids_ti.py: stage 1 the pure elements and stoichiometric cells (18 runs), stage 2 all alloy cells (93 runs: Ni–Al 15 × 3, Ag–Cu x ≤ 0.25 and ≥ 0.75, 16 × 3). GRACE-FS ran on the mygardenx2 CPU (12 ranks × 2 runs, 1.4 times the speed of a GPU), the others on the 2 GPUs. The Ag–Cu liquids were extended to 750 K (pure Cu crystallises partway for all three, so it stops at 1100 K).
